lastRelease.name: v0.20.0
lastRelease.body:
### Added

- Assemble regular-mesh R2S photon sources from caller-supplied zone spectra
  and voxel–zone intersection volumes. Allocation reports include coverage,
  unassigned volume and conservation by zone and energy group.
- Opt-in `nucleide.unfold.staysl_correlated` uses caller-supplied measurement
  covariance in a bounded nonnegative fit and reports measurement chi-square
  and convergence diagnostics.
- `nucleide.spectroscopy.gamma_line_activity` estimates signed activity and
  counting standard uncertainty in Bq from a known gamma peak.
- `nucleide.openmc` reads three-dimensional rectilinear tally meshes and
  calculates C-order geometric voxel volumes from their exact faces.
- Browser demos for mixed-voxel photon sources, gamma-line activity and
  correlated spectrum unfolding call the shared Rust kernels through WASM.
- Full five-level FESTIM 2.1 validation for combined trapping and outlet
  recombination, with measured refinement, parity and mass-balance results.

### Fixed

- OpenMC statepoint extraction recognizes paired energy bounds and indexes
  expanded tally data using the filter order in OpenMC 0.16.
- Interactive tutorial plots load on the Astro development server.

### Changed

- Photon-source constructors avoid copying dense Rust source tables for
  validation and reuse one report for Python totals. OpenMC extraction
  selects the requested score before creating plain Python lists.
- The spectroscopy tutorial shows decay lines and calibration results in
  labeled tables and highlights the selected SPE file's metadata.

lastRelease.name: v0.3.0
lastRelease.body:
NukeIDE 0.3.0 unifies NukeAI behind one capability catalog, extends safe OpenMC edits to project metadata, advanced settings, and fixed-source sources, adds a parametric CAD component library, and completes a theme-and-accessibility pass across empty states, action menus, and viewers.

### Added

- nuke-ai: safe edits preview and apply OpenMC project name, description, and author changes with confirmation and session-scoped undo.
- openmc-studio: NukeAI reads the run mode and every supported OpenMC settings value before previewing an edit.
- openmc-studio: NukeAI advanced settings edits cover output, particle cutoffs, and kinetics (IFP) with nested-safe undo and IFP/inactive cross-checks.
- openmc-studio: NukeAI previews, applies, and undoes independent OpenMC source add/update/remove edits for fixed-source runs, with a read-only source inventory.
- nuke-cad: parametric components add box, cylinder, tube, sphere, cone, and plate-with-hole templates with editable dimensions and radius/diameter aliases.
- nuke-cad: mechanical component templates add L bracket, flange, stepped shaft, pipe with bore, and bolt-circle plate starters.
- nuke-cad: nuclear component templates add hex cell, control-rod guide tube, and assembly grid plate starters.
- nuke-essentials: a shared compact action menu supports host icons, icon-only triggers, keyboard navigation, focus return, and top/bottom placement.
- nuke-ai: embedded action menus make the read-only context actions visible in the statepoint loader, CAD search launcher, and DAGMC editor.
- nuke-visualizer: the statepoint viewer header and empty loader expose Ask About Context, Explain Statepoint, and Diagnose Statepoint.
- openmc-studio: the DAGMC editor header exposes NukeAI actions while the Simulation tab keeps its validation and run groups.

### Changed

- nuke-ai: the chat prompt, chat tool list, Diagnostics tool list, skill allowlists, and MCP read-only allowlist are generated from one capability catalog, so enabled capabilities cannot silently disappear.
- nuke-cad: component-template count parameters rebuild the requested pattern or hole array at creation time instead of staying at the shipped count.
- nuke-cad: NukeAI actions move beside the floating CAD search launcher and open upward, keeping the ribbon uncluttered and the menu clear of dialogs.
- nuke-cad: Feature Tree uses an indented tree-list glyph, distinct from OpenMC Geometry's cell hierarchy.
- nuke-cad: BOM, Model Outline, and Feature Tree empty states use the shared card, drop duplicate status rows, and offer New CAD Document/Open CAD Viewport actions.
- nuke-visualizer: CSG/DAGMC outlines, Dataset Inspector, and Viewer Settings use the shared empty-state card; OpenMC geometry/tally cards align at the top.
- nuke-visualizer: CSG Outline uses one overlapping-primitives glyph in its empty card, sidebar/tab icon, and Nuke Tools entry, keeping it distinct from OpenMC Geometry.
- nuke-visualizer: OpenMC Geometry uses the same cell-node glyph in its tab, Nuke Tools entry, and empty card.
- nuke-ai: Diagnose CSG Geometry uses the shared CSG primitives glyph instead of the old symbol icon.
- nuke-essentials: the generic code Outline view is closed in the default shell; reopen it from View → Outline for code files.

### Fixed

- nuke-cad: the Appearance opacity field uses the themed input chrome instead of a white native number field, and opacity-only edits keep the theme body color.
- nuke-cad: the duplicate unsaved dot behind the document toolbar is removed; the toolbar's own dot is the single indicator.
- nuke-essentials: the Welcome page scrolls vertically when walkthroughs and recent workspaces exceed the viewport.
- nuke-essentials: recent-workspace rows keep a flat hover surface instead of underlining the path.
- nuke-essentials: illustrated empty-state icons and CAD mask glyphs render at the intended size instead of Theia's 16px codicon default.
- nuke-essentials: shared dialogs, color picker, viewer bar, ViewCube, and view badges expose screen-reader names and keyboard-focus tooltips.
- nuke-ai: NukeAI action menus use an icon-only bot trigger with a tooltip, and dashboard groups use the bot icon and sentence-case labels.
- nuke-ai: detached chat windows keep the NukeAI welcome and tool-card styling.
- openmc-studio: tally and dashboard checkboxes follow the active theme, checkbox labels stay sentence case, and icon-only actions expose screen-reader names.
- nuke-visualizer: probe and find-data cards share one slot without covering each other or the bottom bar, the viewer bar wraps on narrow panels, and icon-only controls expose screen-reader names.

lastRelease.name: v2.3.0
lastRelease.body:
### Added

- Crash-safe recovery foundation: per-process worker heartbeats with container
  incarnation identity, fenced operation heartbeats, and active approval reuse.
  Heartbeat age is an inspection trigger only; it never releases reservations
  or proves termination by itself.
- Registry-verified environment identity: bounded OCI/Docker registry
  resolution with Bearer/Basic authentication, exact platform manifest digest
  proof, optional registry-verified pulls, and a portable environment
  fingerprint for cross-install matching. Tag movement never creates a new
  approval automatically.
- A range-scoped signed-commit check for pull requests, pushes and release
  tags, so legacy unsigned history does not block new work.
- Cross-install environment manifests now match destination approvals by the
  portable fingerprint only; local-only manifests keep strict local revision
  matching. Admin operations visibility adds sanitized list/detail views and a
  proof-only reconcile action with no force path.
- `doctor` now reports recovery-journal, heartbeat, registry-verification,
  credential, and legacy-row state without mutating the stack.
- External Dockerfile base images are now checked by a strict `Base Image
  Pinning` security job included in `Security Gate`; a weekly review reports
  upstream tag drift in one tracked issue.
- Tagged release CI publishes deterministic CycloneDX SBOMs plus build
  provenance and SBOM attestations for every image, then verifies them with
  `gh attestation verify`. Normal branch CI does not run the release-only
  scans.
- Operators get a read-only cross-owner queue view, and owners get deduplicated
  recovery attention/completion notifications plus a bounded daily reminder
  for unresolved recovery-required work. Queue rows include sanitized
  owner/environment/plan names, requested resources and status summaries; the
  owner filter uses a directory picker when the operator can read users.
- Recovery operations show sanitized target and owner names, and environment
  revision history supports loaded-page portability/revocation filters, search,
  and copyable full IDs, fingerprints and manifest digests.
- Recovery metrics and alerts cover worker-heartbeat freshness, recovery-scan
  health, stalled or recovery-required operations, and registry-verification
  gaps. Scan freshness is persisted so the backend scrape reports work that ran
  in the Celery process.
- Queue `starting` requests are mapped to their launch operation. An orphaned
  request stays operator-visible until runtime absence is proved, and work is
  never blindly requeued or cancelled.
- A backup artifact cleanup interrupted after its durable `delete:<uuid>` claim
  is recovered only after the claimant is proven stopped; the retry rechecks
  mounts and either removes the artifact or records `delete_failed`.
- Volume backup/restore execution now heartbeats under its fenced operation,
  and proof-backed completion is applied by the reconciler only after artifact
  and helper-termination checks. The admin UI adds environment-revision and
  recovery-operation consoles; the console has no force or override path.
- A launch left `uncertain` by a crash may be adopted as success only when
  complete runtime and public-readiness proof is available; otherwise it stays
  protected for operator reconciliation.

### Changed

- Mobile page content and the bottom navigation dock respect iOS safe-area
  insets, so the last controls remain scrollable above the dock.
- Recovery scans now use partial indexes matching the active launch, backup and
  restore selection order. On a 100k/50k/50k seeded journal the three-query
  p95 dropped from 16.9 ms to 2.4 ms, so the 30-second scan no longer reads
  completed history.
- The root README architecture map is now a generated light/dark SVG pair
  selected by `<picture>`, with local brand icons embedded as data URIs and no
  CDN or runtime network dependency. The old HTML/PNG source was removed and
  docs CI verifies the generated SVGs against their checked-in generator.

### Security

- Updated the frontend nginx base to 1.31.9 with Alpine package upgrades, moved
  the shared environment base to Debian 13.7 and require
  `nginx >= 1.26.3-3+deb13u11`, and rebuilt the auth sidecar with Go 1.27.4.
  This picks up the nginx2root and related DSA-6642-1 fixes (CVE-2026-123007,
  CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-113425,
  CVE-2026-118899) plus current Go standard-library fixes.
- Upgraded Traefik from the end-of-life 3.6 line to 3.7.19, including fixes for
  the HTTP/1 opaque request-target routing/auth bypass, CONNECT connection-pool
  poisoning, and ReplacePathRegex traversal advisories. Enabled
  `global.aliasHeadersStrategy: delete` and bounded monitoring ForwardAuth
  response bodies.
- Refreshed frontend lockfile dependencies to clear all `npm audit` findings,
  including the seroval deserialization issue.
- Updated the backend runtime base to Python 3.13.18 on Debian 13.7, PyJWT
  2.14.0, and msgpack 1.2.3, and removed the unused pip/setuptools tools from
  shipped backend and volume-helper images. Trivy now reports no fixed
  HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities in either image.


## Container images

| Image | Tag |
|-------|-----|
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-backend` | `2.3.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-frontend` | `2.3.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-auth-sidecar` | `2.3.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-volume-helper` | `2.3.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-base` | `2.3.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-conda-base` | `2.3.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-workspace` | `2.3.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-dev` | `2.3.0` |

All images are also tagged as `latest`.

### Pull all images

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-backend:2.3.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-frontend:2.3.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-auth-sidecar:2.3.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-volume-helper:2.3.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-base:2.3.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-conda-base:2.3.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-workspace:2.3.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-dev:2.3.0
```

### Attestations

On a successful tagged CI/CD run, build provenance and CycloneDX SBOM attestations
are published for every image above. The release workflow then verifies all application
images and the environment base image with `gh attestation verify`. No SLSA level is claimed.

```bash
gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-backend@sha256:<digest> --repo nukehub-dev/nukelab
gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-backend@sha256:<digest> --repo nukehub-dev/nukelab --predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom
```
